Hi Priya / Anil — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get you a tight pilot quote.

Recap from our call:
- Pilot objective: validate conversational triage + short-form summarization for patient intake flows.
- Desired SLO: 95th percentile latency <= 400ms for interactive flows; throughputs during business hours will peak.
- Current model preference: open model you mentioned (gptx-optimized) — we'll confirm compatibility in onboarding.

Two quick asks so we size batching/concurrency appropriately and give a target unit price: please confirm the following in a quick reply or by filling the attached one-pager (redwood-pilot-estimate.xlsx):
1) Expected token volumes: average tokens per request and daily/weekly totals (sample numbers are fine).
2) Burst profile: steady stream vs. concentrated bursts (hour windows, % of daily volume in top hour).
3) Concurrency expectations: average active requests and peak concurrent requests.
4) Target unit economics: target $/1M tokens you consider acceptable for the pilot (helps us pick hosted vs dedicated options).

Notes on batching/latency tradeoffs we discussed: continuous batching can lower per-token infer cost by aggregating in-flight requests (we typically see 20–45% savings depending on prompt reuse and request size) but it requires tuning of the batching window and max_batch to honor latency SLOs. We'll propose two pilot options once we have the numbers: hosted (dynamic batching) and dedicated reserved (predictable latency + lower unit price with commitments).

I attached a blank estimate to make it quick — if you prefer, paste numbers into a reply. I'll pull Marcus and Monica in to run the cost math as soon as we have the numbers.

Next steps we propose if numbers look reasonable:
- You return sample traffic / estimates (or the attached completed).
- Redwood provides a 30-day pilot quote with two price options and a recommended batching config.
- If acceptable, sign the pilot MOU and we spin up a sandbox.

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

Lauren / Marcus — quick back-of-envelope on Priya's numbers and what we should propose.

Inputs from Priya:
- Baseline: 2M tokens/day -> ~60M tokens/month.
- Peak could push to 85M/month in bursty weeks.
- Avg request 420 tokens, KV hit ~65%, concurrency avg 45 / peak 120.
- Greenfield target: ~$9 / 1M tokens for hosted pilot; $6–7 / 1M if dedicated. Budget 6k–10k/mo.

Rough cost math (hosted dynamic batching):
- If we price at $12 / 1M tokens (midpoint offer), 60M tokens -> $720 / month; 85M -> $1,020 / month. That fits their stated budget range easily.
- If we price at $9 / 1M tokens exactly: 60M -> $540 / month; 85M -> $765 / month.

Important caveats and assumptions:
- Continuous batching savings: expect 25–40% reduction in GPU-seconds per token vs naive request-per-call if batching window is tuned. The realization depends on concurrency smoothing and prefix reuse.
- Latency tradeoff: to hold 95th <= 400ms with peaks up to 120 concurrent, we should target a short batching window (6–12ms) and an aggressive max_batch around 64–128 for the model family they want. That will preserve tail latency while still getting most batching gains.
- KV cache reuse (65%): reduces per-request compute for multi-turns but doesn't shrink initial prompt compute — good for cost.
- Peak protection: recommend including burst capacity (short autoscale headroom) or temporary dedicated slots for the morning window to avoid steady-state contention.

Proposal options to present:
1) Hosted pilot — dynamic batching, no commit: $12 / 1M tokens, 95th latency target 380–400ms, continuous batching with T=8ms window and max_batch=96 (default tuned). Includes up to 2x baseline autoscale burst for morning window.
2) Dedicated reserved pilot — 3 month minimum commit, $7.50 / 1M tokens effective, lower instance-level overhead, dedicated GPUs with guaranteed concurrency headroom and 95th <= 350ms.

I'll draft numbers into the estimate sheet and attach a sample pilot MOU for Lauren to send. Also flagging that if their true monthly total is closer to 85M, the dedicated route produces bigger savings and stronger latency guarantees.

— Monica
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
